hypothesis_or_artifact: The BTC premium "decay" finding and the instruction it generates to a successor against relying on the measured premium
label: DERIVED
claim_quote: **BTC is significant in every quarter but decaying monotonically — down 60.4% across the sample.** A reader planning around this should assume the decay continues rather than that the average persists.
evidence_summary: The four quarterly BTC means and t statistics are published with their n in the stored sealed-read artifact: 284.53 bps (t 3.498, n 488), 250.587 (t 3.845, n 488), 145.132 (t 2.619, n 488), 112.719 (t 2.098, n 491). No test of the decay is performed anywhere in the repository; the claim rests on the ordering of four point estimates and their ratio, and is converted into an imperative to a successor ("Do not read the BTC premium as stationary"). Cochran's Q on the same four numbers gives Q = 4.784 on 3 df, p = 0.188 — the quarterly means are not distinguishable from a common mean. The Q1-Q4 difference is 171.8 bps with SE 97.5 bps (z = 1.762, two-sided p = 0.078). By contrast the ETH quarters, where the repository draws a conclusion of the same kind, do reject homogeneity (Q = 9.789, 3 df, p = 0.020), so the method is not hostile to the repository's conclusions in general.
recomputation: Standard errors backed out of the stored (mean, t) pairs as SE = mean/t: BTC 0.035559, 0.028491, 0.024226, 0.023488 vol points. Cochran's Q with inverse-variance weights, 3 df: BTC Q = 4.784, p = 0.1883 (pooled mean 0.077763 vol pts); ETH Q = 9.789, p = 0.0204. Two-sample z on Q1-Q4: BTC diff 0.075110 vol pts = 171.81 bps, SE 0.042616 = 97.48 bps, z = 1.762, two-sided p = 0.0780, one-sided p = 0.0390. P(monotone ordering of four exchangeable draws) = 1/24 = 4.2%.
would_resolve: Run and report a heterogeneity or trend test on the quarterly means, and downgrade "assume the decay continues" to "the point estimates decline monotonically; a formal test on the same four numbers does not reject a constant premium (Q = 4.78, 3 df, p = 0.19), so the decline is suggestive and not established."

hypothesis_or_artifact: The 49.61 bps reopen threshold on the one open MBT route
label: READ
claim_quote: | **All-in MBT option + futures bid-ask, plus CME exchange and regulatory fees**, at the pessimistic (90th-percentile) end | **≤ 49.61 bps of notional** | The room between the BTC premium's one-sided 95% lower bound (142.740 bps) and twice the measured commission-only pessimistic cost (2 × 21.760 = 43.520 bps) |
evidence_summary: The stated description and the stated number are different quantities. "The room between 142.740 and 43.520" is 99.220 bps. The figure actually used, 49.61 bps, is 142.740/2 - 21.760, i.e. the room in cost space once the registered rule premium_CI_lower >= 2.0 x cost_pessimistic is inverted. The number is right and the sentence explaining it is wrong, in all three places the threshold is published. An operator applying the description as written would carry a budget exactly 2x too large and could report the open route as clearing when it does not. Inputs: BTC CI lower bound 142.7401 bps (n = 1,955) and MBT pessimistic commission-only cost 21.760 bps.
recomputation: 142.740 - 43.520 = 99.220 bps (the published description). 142.740/2 - 21.760 = 49.610 bps (the published number). The intended derivation reproduces 49.610 exactly.
